div.head: Rect 10, 10.1
div.ab: [10] Be folgeran. Folgere gebyreð, þæt he on twelf monðum II æceras geearnige, oðerne gesawene 7 oðerne unsawene; sædige sylf ðæne; 7 his mete 7 scoung 7 glofung him gebyreð. [10.1] Gyf he mare geearnian mæig, him bið sylfum fremu.

[10] Folgario competit, ut in duodecim mensibus II acras habeat, unam seminatam, aliam non; sed idem seminet eam; et uictum suum et calciamenta debet habere et cirothecas. [10.1] Si plus deseruit, ipsi commodum erit.

be folgeran . Folgere gebyreð þæt he ontwelf Monðum .ii . æceras geearnige oðerne gesawene 7 oðerne unsawene sædige sylf ðæne . 7 his mete . 7 scoung 7 glofung him gebyreð gyf he mare gearnian mæig him bið sylfum fremu.

Be folgeran Folgere gebyreð, þæt he on twelf monðum II æceras geearnige, oðerne gesawene and oðerne unsawene—sædige sylf ðæne—and his mete and scoung and glofung him gebyreð. [10.1] Gyf he mare geearnian mæig, him bið sylfum fremu.

[10] Von Gefolgsleuten [bei der herrschaftlichen Domäne]. Dem Gefolgsmanne kommt zu, dass er in 12 Monaten [Dienst] zwei Äcker verdiene, einen besät und den anderen unbesät; diesen säe er selbst; und seine Beköstigung und Empfang von Schuhen und Handschuhen gebührt ihm. [10.1] Wenn er mehr zu verdienen vermag, ist es ihm selber ein Vortheil.

[10] Of [household] followers [on the lord's demesne]. It is due to the follower that he earn two acres in 12 months [of service], one sown and the other unsown; the latter let him sow himself; and his food and the receiving of shoes and gloves are due to him. [10.1] If he can earn more, it is to his own advantage.

Concerning the follower [of the plough] For the follower [of the plough] it is fitting that he earns two acres in twelve months, the one sown and the other unsown that [he should] sow it himself, and his food and shoes and gloves are due to him; if he ploughs more may it be to his own advantage.

Regarding the Plowman For the plowman, it is appropriate that he earn two acres per year, one sown and the other unsown—he must sow it himself—and his food and his shoes and gloves are due to him. [10.1] If he can earn more for himself, it will be for his own benefit.
div.note: This row combines Liebermann's 10–10.1. K: ‘gearnian’ corrected to ‘geearnian’. The Quadripartitus MS T reads ‘ethem.’ for 9.1 ‘ehtemannis’ (confused with ‘eahta’ II Atr 5.2). Liebermann compares Rect 12.
